subject: Staging window for deferred deletion: backup purge & log exception request
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@datacust.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staging window for deferred deletion: backup purge & log exception request

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing a scheduled irreversible purge of several backup tiers that include partial copies of customer datasets. Before we proceed we'd like to confirm Redwood's acceptance of a temporary "staging window" (45 days) where backups are logically marked for deletion but retained on cold storage to allow restores and forensics.

Key points: 
- Scope: cold backups and archival snapshots only (no active production stores).
- Staging window: 45 days after which backups are overwritten/crypto-erased.
- Logs: we request a scoped log-retention exception to retain ingestion and troubleshooting logs for up to 90 days (explicitly excluding downstream PII payloads).
- Deletion mechanism: we will perform cryptographic key destruction where feasible; we can provide attestations.

Attached is our purge plan (datacust-purge-plan.pdf) and a proposed DPA amendment (see datacust-dpa-amendment-proposal.docx). Who is the right contact on your side to discuss a subprocessor-level exception and the DPA language?

Regards,
Tom Narayan
Ops Lead — DataCust
ops@datacust.com

Attachment: datacust-purge-plan.pdf (PDF 210KB)
Attachment: datacust-dpa-amendment-proposal.docx (DOCX 34KB)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@datacust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staging window for deferred deletion: backup purge & log exception request

Tom — thanks for the details and the attachments. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marcus (security) plus Lauren (product) so we can cover all angles. A few clarifying questions from infra/security: 

1) Can you confirm the exact dataset identifiers / buckets that will be subject to the staging window? We need per-dataset timelines rather than a blanket policy.
2) For the 45-day staging, is there a programmatic purge API we can call to request immediate removal in support tickets or legal holds? If not, we'll need an operational runbook and SLAs for ad-hoc erasure.
3) Your note about cryptographic key destruction is promising — will you provide a timeline and attestation for key shredding vs physical overwrite?
4) Regarding logs: we need a narrow scoping statement describing which log types are requested for 90 days (e.g., ingestion logs, routing traces) and an assurance that PII is redacted.

Preliminarily from a product standpoint we may be able to accept a staggered deletion model for cold backups if it's limited to the proposed buckets and if we receive: (a) an API for purge requests, (b) an attestation template, and (c) a signed DPA amendment.

Kimberly — can you advise on DPA amendment language and whether Redwood can sign an exception limited to a named subprocessor? Marcus — can security greenlight a 45-day staging for cold backups only?

Thanks — Dylan
Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Thanks Tom and Dylan. A few legal points up front: 

- Redwood can consider a narrowly scoped DPA amendment that documents a limited staging window for specific named buckets/snapshots for the purpose of restores/forensics. The amendment must include: dataset identifiers, TTL (45 days), and the conditions under which Redwood may require immediate purge (court order/legal hold).
- For logs: any exception must be narrowly scoped (types and retention) and we need a technical description that shows PII is not retained in those logs. We will not approve a blanket 90-day retention that includes content payloads.
- We will require either (1) an annual attestation and SOC2 evidence showing the subprocessors' controls, or (2) a one-time third-party attestation for the purge run if the 45-day exception is granted.

Please upload redlines to the Drive folder (I created a template) and provide the DocuSign link for the amendment.

Next steps for DataCust: provide the per-bucket list, the attestation template, and the DocuSign envelope. On our side I will circulate a DPA amendment draft by EOD Friday.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Staging window for deferred deletion: backup purge & log exception request

Hi Kimberly / Dylan / Marcus / Lauren,

Thanks — answers below and we've uploaded supporting docs to the Drive link you provided.

- Scope: staging applies only to cold backups and offsite archival snapshots for the following buckets: dc-prod-backups-2022, dc-prod-backups-2023, dc-snapshots-arch-01 (we included object prefixes in the Drive doc). Active production stores and customer-facing indexes are not included.
- API: We currently have an internal purge endpoint used by our compliance team. We are prepared to expose a scoped, authenticated purge API for Redwood that will accept a purge token and return an audit ID. We'll share API spec in the Drive folder.
- Deletion mechanism: For the archived tier we will perform cryptographic key destruction within 24–72 hours after the 45-day staging expires. For certain legacy tapes where crypto-erase isn't supported we will perform physical overwrite or verified decommissioning; details in the attached plan.
- Logs: the 90-day request is limited to ingestion metadata and routing traces. No payloads or extracted PII will be retained; we will apply PII redaction prior to retention and will share our redaction log.

DocuSign link for the proposed amendment: https://docusign.net/00A1B2C3/datacust-dpa (envelope 00A1B2C3).

We also included a sample attestation for key destruction and a proposed audit timeline. Attachment: datacust-dpa-amendment-proposal.docx

Are the items above sufficient for your legal and security review? Happy to set a short call if needed.

Best,
Tom Narayan
Ops Lead — DataCust
ops@datacust.com

Tom — appreciate the fast responses and the materials. Summary and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Security: Marcus will review the Drive artifacts and the API spec. We need the purge API to provide an audit ID and a signed attestation payload after deletion; otherwise we will not approve automated purges. Marcus — please respond by EOD Monday if you see any blocking issues.
2) Legal: Kimberly to circulate Redwood's DPA amendment draft. DataCust to push redlines to the Drive folder and execute via DocuSign link provided. Deadline for signed amendment: 2025-08-29 to avoid delaying the purge window.
3) Product/Operations: Lauren, please confirm that our internal ticketing can accept the purge audit ID and that we can surface it in customer support flows. Lauren — can you confirm by Monday?

Assuming those items are met (API w/ audit ID, attestation, signed amendment limited to named buckets), Redwood can provisionally approve a staggered 45-day staging window for the listed cold backups and a scoped 90-day ingestion-log retention for troubleshooting. This approval is conditional and will be revoked if any of the above artifacts are not provided or if PII is present in the scoped logs.

I'll hold a short call if DataCust prefers to walk through the API spec and attestation flow — otherwise we'll proceed with the outlined tasks.

Thanks — Dylan
